summary: The note examines the labor shortage facing small businesses, focused on attracting mid-career professionals, and lays out strategies drawn from small business leaders. These include building an employer brand, investing in employee development, offering flexibility and technology, engaging the community, competitive pay and benefits, streamlined hiring, diversity, and employee referrals. It concludes that a multifaceted approach centered on human capital helps small businesses survive and thrive.
one_line: Small businesses can address labor shortages and attract mid-career talent through employer branding, development, flexibility, community ties, benefits, streamlined hiring, diversity, and referrals.
key_facts: Since September 1, 2023, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reports a 4% decrease in workforce participation compared to the previous decade.
Experts attribute the labor shortage to baby boomer retirements, shifting career expectations among millennials and Gen Z, and lingering effects of the pandemic-era work-from-home trend.
Sarah James of James & Co. said the problem is not the number of applications but the lack of suitable candidates with the right blend of experience and readiness.
Michael Peters, Founder of TechSolutions, said the company pivoted its message to show it values people and their growth, using employee testimonials, career growth stories, and work-life balance.
Anna Roberts, HR Director at GreenLeaf Designs, said the company focuses on growing talent through training programs, mentorship initiatives, and clear paths to advancement.

Edward Gomez, CEO of cybersecurity startup VirtualSpear, called flexibility 'a game changer for attracting the talent pool that values autonomy'; tools like Slack, Zoom, and Asana enable remote collaboration.
Lisa Tran, co-owner of Tran's Bakery, said community connections are a rich source of talent and create mutual loyalty.
Small businesses can build community visibility by joining community events, sponsoring local programs, and partnering with community colleges and training centers.
Profit-sharing, health and wellness incentives, and retirement plans can distinguish a small business; Jordan Keats, CFO at Green Homes Inc., stressed a 'total package'.
Blue Dot Media streamlined hiring by reducing touchpoints to reach decisions faster, according to HR manager Tammy Nguyen.
TechSolutions has seen growth in innovative ideas since committing to diversifying its workforce.
Employee referral programs can reduce recruitment costs and shorten the hiring timeline; James says employees are 'fantastic scouts for culture fit'.
